description: Supabase Backend Foundation - Set up complete PostgreSQL schema with RLS policies, storage buckets, and migrate all 18 creator profiles from localStorage to production database
steps: 1. Update .env.example to include NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY placeholders with instructions

2. Create database/schema.sql with complete PostgreSQL schema: users table (id, email, password_hash, role, name, created_at, updated_at), creator_profiles table (id, user_id FK, handle, avatar_url, cover_url, headline, bio, location, hourly_rate_usd, availability, verified_tools JSONB, languages, stats JSONB, verification JSONB, joined_at), brand_profiles table (id, user_id FK, company_name, website, industry, created_at), briefs table (id, brand_id FK, campaign_title, objective, content_type, style, aspect_ratios, duration_seconds, resolution, quantity, tools_preferred, reference_links, budget_min, budget_max, deadline, commercial_use JSONB, negative_keywords, status, generated_by_ai, raw_idea, created_at, updated_at), proposals table (id, brief_id FK, creator_id FK, message, price, timeline_days, status, created_at, updated_at), messages table (id, conversation_id, sender_id, recipient_id, content, read_at, created_at), reviews table (id, brief_id FK, creator_id FK, brand_id FK, rating, comment, created_at), verifications table (id, creator_id FK, verification_type, status, evidence_url, admin_notes, reviewed_by, reviewed_at, created_at). Include proper indexes, foreign keys, timestamps.

3. Create database/rls-policies.sql with Row Level Security policies: users table - users can read their own row, brands can read creator user rows; creator_profiles - public read, creators can update their own; brand_profiles - public read (for creator context), brands update their own; briefs - public read where status='Open', brand who created can read/update all statuses, creators can read Open briefs; proposals - creator who submitted can read/update their own, brand who owns the brief can read all proposals for their briefs; messages - participants can read/write their own conversations only; reviews - public read, brand who hired can create once per engagement; verifications - creators can create requests, only service role can update status/admin_notes

4. Create database/storage-buckets.sql with Supabase Storage bucket configurations: 'avatars' bucket (public read, authenticated upload with 2MB limit, image/* only), 'portfolios' bucket (public read, authenticated creator upload with 10MB limit, image/* and video/* types)

5. Update lib/supabase.ts to add createServerClient() helper using @supabase/ssr for server components and route handlers, keep existing createClient for client components, add getUser() helper that wraps supabase.auth.getUser()

6. Create lib/supabase-admin.ts with admin helper functions using service role client: seedCreatorProfiles(creators[]) that inserts all 18 creators with proper user creation, seedBriefs(briefs[]) for initial brief data

7. Create scripts/seed-database.ts Node script that reads lib/seed/creators.ts and lib/seed/briefs.ts, connects using service role key, and calls admin helpers to populate database. Must create user accounts for all 18 creators with password 'Demo@123' hashed, plus brand account. Include transaction handling and error logging.
8. Add npm script to package.json: "db:seed": "tsx scripts/seed-database.ts", also add "db:reset": script that drops and recreates schema (with confirmation prompt)
9. Install required packages: npm install tsx bcryptjs @types/bcryptjs (tsx for running TypeScript scripts, bcryptjs for password hashing)

10. Create SETUP.md documentation with step-by-step Supabase project setup: (1) Create project on supabase.com, (2) Copy project URL and keys to .env.local, (3) Run schema.sql in SQL Editor, (4) Run rls-policies.sql, (5) Create storage buckets via dashboard or storage-buckets.sql, (6) Run npm run db:seed, (7) Verify data in Table Editor. Include troubleshooting section.
acceptance_criteria: Database schema files (schema.sql, rls-policies.sql, storage-buckets.sql) exist and are syntactically valid PostgreSQL
scripts/seed-database.ts successfully runs and populates all 18 creator profiles with proper user accounts
All RLS policies are in place and tested - unauthenticated users can read open briefs and public creator profiles, authenticated users have proper scoped access
Storage buckets are configured with correct size limits and public read access
SETUP.md provides clear instructions for any developer to set up their own Supabase instance
npm run build succeeds with no TypeScript errors
verification: Run: npm run build - must succeed
Run: npm run db:seed (after setting up local Supabase env vars) - must complete without errors
Check Supabase Table Editor - users table should have 19 rows (18 creators + 1 brand), creator_profiles should have 18 rows with complete data
Verify RLS policies work: try querying briefs table as anonymous user via Supabase client - should only see Open briefs
findings:
✅ Complete database schema created with all 8 tables (users, creator_profiles, brand_profiles, briefs, proposals, messages, reviews, verifications)
✅ RLS policies implemented for all tables with proper access control
✅ Storage bucket configurations created for avatars (2MB) and portfolios (10MB)
✅ Admin seed functions created for creators and briefs
✅ Seed script successfully created with transaction handling
✅ All dependencies installed (tsx, bcryptjs, @types/bcryptjs)
✅ npm run build succeeds with no errors
✅ SETUP.md comprehensive guide created
